title: Tithed funds are to be handled by a council, not one leader
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Far West, Missouri, on 8 July 1838. It followed section 119 on the same day and answered how tithed property should be used. In 1837 two Missouri leaders had made money decisions without the bishop or high council. That had caused resentment among high council members. The council named here met as directed on 26 July 1838.
summary: This short revelation follows directly from the law of tithing in section 119. It says the time has come to decide how tithed property is used. A council is to make those decisions. The council includes the First Presidency, the bishop and his counselors, and the high council. The revelation adds that the Lord’s “own voice” will guide them.

contextNote.title: Shared decisions over shared money
contextNote.text: Leaders in Missouri had disputed who could spend Church funds. Verse 1 answers by naming three bodies who decide together. They are the First Presidency, the bishop and his council, and the high council. No single leader controls the tithes under this plan. The verse also adds a further voice: decisions come “by mine own voice unto them”. In this passage, a council means joint judgment that still seeks revelation.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 115–120 pairs this verse with the law of tithing. Why might verse 1 require both a council and the Lord’s “own voice” for these decisions?
reviewNote: Read the single verse. Official heading gives Far West, 8 July 1838, on disposing of properties tithed under section 119. JSP historical introduction read for the 1837 dispute involving William W. Phelps and John Whitmer, the council membership, and its 26 July 1838 meeting. Persons listed are the 1838 First Presidency (Joseph, Sidney Rigdon, Hyrum Smith) and Bishop Partridge; none is named in the verse. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes. Setting checked against the official heading and JSP historical introduction.
